text.paragraph: Periodic adult preventive visit after cancer treatment. [S]

Ms. Perón is a 32-year-old foundation director who comes for her yearly preventive visit, four and a half months after finishing chemoradiation and brachytherapy for stage IIB squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix. Her PET-CT a month ago showed a complete metabolic response. She is back at work full time. The estradiol patch and nightly progesterone have stopped the hot flashes and night sweats, and she uses the vaginal dilator three times a week. Her energy is nearly normal, and she finished the iron course last month. She meets the oncology social worker monthly. She asks what else she should be doing to stay well. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-09-21; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 52.8 kg, BMI 19.4; blood pressure 110/70
Radiation field healed; no suspicious lesions

Bleeding after intercourse and between periods, with heavier periods, for about four months, with tiredness and a dull pelvic ache. Never had cervical screening. Speculum examination shows a friable, exophytic mass about 4 cm across on the cervix that bleeds on contact. Punch biopsy, HPV test and cytology taken; urgent gynecologic oncology consultation booked
S — Synthetic presenting problem linked to her documented abnormal bleeding with anemia; superseded by the diagnosis at the consultation.
Iron deficiency anemia from chronic blood loss: hemoglobin 9.4 g/dL, mean cell volume 72 fL, ferritin 6 ng/mL, with tiredness and breathlessness on stairs
S — Synthetic modern finding linked to her documented anemia from vaginal bleeding.

Invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix, HPV 16 positive: an exophytic tumor about 4.5 cm across with clinical involvement of the left parametrium, not reaching the pelvic wall; pelvic MRI and PET-CT ordered for FIGO 2018 staging. Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented cervical cancer
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the gynecologic oncology consultation.

Acute cystitis during pelvic chemoradiation: two days of new burning, urgency and cloudy urine on top of mild radiation frequency, without fever or flank pain; urine dipstick positive for leukocyte esterase and nitrite; culture grew Escherichia coli sensitive to nitrofurantoin; neutrophil count and kidney function normal; resolved
S — Synthetic acute infection; not a historical claim.
Ovarian failure after pelvic radiation, with hot flashes, night sweats, poor sleep and vaginal dryness two weeks after treatment; FSH 72 mIU/mL and estradiol 14 pg/mL
S — Synthetic expected effect of pelvic chemoradiation.

Periodic adult preventive visit completed. Health risk assessment reviewed and the prevention plan updated for a cancer survivor. Cervical screening is replaced by her gynecologic oncology surveillance. HIV and hepatitis C tests at diagnosis were negative. Influenza vaccine given today. The HPV vaccine was discussed: at 32 it is a shared decision, and it would not treat her cancer; she declined. Pelvic radiation has ended the possibility of pregnancy, so no contraception is needed. [S]
Influenza vaccine today.
Calcium-rich diet and weight-bearing exercise; estrogen therapy protects bone.
Next preventive visit in one year.

Squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix, FIGO 2018 stage IIB (C53.9). No evidence of disease four and a half months after treatment. [S]
Gynecologic oncology review every three months for two years.
Report vaginal bleeding, pelvic or back pain, leg swelling, or weight loss without waiting.

Ovarian failure after pelvic radiation (E89.41). Symptoms controlled on estradiol 0.1 mg patch twice weekly with progesterone 100 mg nightly; blood pressure normal; no clot symptoms. [S]
Continue until about the usual age of menopause, reviewed yearly.

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 18 minutes, in Spanish, with her consent. She named a health care agent, recorded in the confidential part of the chart and not named here. She said that she always wants to be told the truth about her illness herself, first and fully, and that if her cancer ever returned and could not be cured she would want care focused on comfort and on being able to keep working as long as possible. She asked that her wishes be written in Spanish as well as English. To be revisited yearly or if her health changes. [S]
